overall_summary: The channel is experiencing a clear performance surge in the space and exoplanet mystery niche, with videos featuring extreme planetary conditions (e.g., burning ice, coal-dark planets, ruby rain) consistently gaining the highest views and engagement. Conversely, repetitive psychology and brain facts are failing to capture audience interest, showing extremely low view counts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' (1,055 views) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,018 views) are the top performers, driven by high-contrast, mind-bending cosmic concepts.
winning_patterns.action: Focus content creation on highly visual, extreme space phenomena and bizarre exoplanets with paradoxical physical properties.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' yielded single-digit or low double-digit views (5, 11, 53 views), and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' got only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Discontinue generic psychology facts and avoid re-uploading identical concepts without significant hook variations.

next_video.concept: The tidally locked planet where one half is a boiling lava ocean and the other half is a frozen wasteland of ice.
next_video.opening_direction: Show a split screen of liquid fire and absolute-zero ice, asking: 'What if you lived on a planet where you could freeze and burn to death at the exact same time?'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the boundary line between these two halves creates a permanent, apocalyptic supersonic windstorm that rains vaporized rock.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful exoplanet anomaly trend, utilizing the same high-contrast, paradoxical hook style that made the 'Burning Ice' video a top performer.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' scenario format applied to these extreme exoplanets (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Liquid Diamond?') to see if adding a hypothetical first-person narrative increases viewer retention compared to standard third-person fact delivery.
